notes.meaning: King Hezekiah chose trusted scribes to gather and write down these proverbs of Solomon hundreds of years after Solomon lived. God led these men to preserve His wisdom so the people could learn how to honor Him. These sayings provide practical guidance for government rulers and everyday life.

God's wisdom and decisions are far deeper than human minds can grasp, and this mystery shows His supreme majesty. Good human rulers, however, earn honor by looking closely into difficult matters and uncovering hidden crimes. Leaders must study issues carefully instead of acting in ignorance.

No person can easily reach the highest heavens or measure the deepest parts of the earth. In a similar way, ordinary people cannot easily know what is inside a king's heart. Leaders must often keep their plans and state matters private to govern wisely.

A silversmith must melt away worthless impurities before he can craft a fine silver vessel. In the same way, a king must remove wicked advisers and corrupt officials from his royal court. When bad influences are cleared away, the government stands firm in justice.

People should not push themselves forward into places of honor at court or act grand before great men. It is far better to be invited up to a better seat than to be publicly demoted before everyone. True humility protects us from deep embarrassment and earns real honor.

A person should never rush to court to start a heated lawsuit against someone else. If your neighbor proves you wrong, you will end up humiliated and ruined by legal troubles. It is much wiser to pause and consider the facts before starting a fight.

When you have a disagreement with a neighbor, talk it out with him in private first. Never blab another person's private business to the public just to win an argument. If you betray someone's trust, people will call you an unfaithful gossip and you will never shake off the shame.

Choosing the right words for the right moment is a thing of great beauty. It is like golden fruit served inside beautiful baskets made of silver network. Wise and timely speech brings refreshment to everyone who hears it.

A wise correction spoken with care is as valuable as an ornament of fine gold. When a teachable person listens and takes that correction to heart, their life becomes truly adorned with wisdom. Accepting guidance with a humble mind is a sign of good sense.

During the scorching heat of harvest, a cold drink chilled with mountain snow brings deep relief to tired workers. In the same way, a dependable messenger who does his job faithfully brings joy and peace of mind to his master. Reliable workers are a rare and refreshing gift.

In a dry land, gathering clouds and wind make farmers hope for rain, but empty clouds bring only bitter disappointment. A person who loudly boasts about gifts he never gives or makes promises he does not keep is just like that. Bragging about empty promises destroys trust.

Patiently waiting for the right moment can win over even a stubborn ruler or powerful judge. Soft, gentle words have a quiet power that can break down hard, stubborn opposition like snapping a bone. Calm kindness achieves far more than angry shouting.

Honey is sweet and healthy, but eating too much of it will make you sick to your stomach. God lets us enjoy the good things of this world, but He calls us to use them with moderation. Self-control keeps good pleasures from turning harmful.

Being a friendly neighbor is good, but showing up at someone's house too often will wear them out. If you interrupt their daily affairs and overstay your welcome, their warm friendship can quickly turn to irritation. Keeping a sensible balance shows respect for others.

Lying about a neighbor in court or spreading rumors is as cruel as an attack with deadly weapons. Whether striking close like a club and sword or from a distance like an arrow, dishonest words destroy a person's life and good name. A lying tongue inflicts terrible harm.

Trying to chew with a cracked tooth or walk on a dislocated foot causes sudden, severe pain instead of help. Counting on an untrustworthy person during a crisis brings that exact kind of painful disappointment. We must be very careful about whom we trust when trouble arrives.

Taking someone's coat away in freezing weather leaves them shivering, and pouring vinegar on soda ruins it with harsh fizzing. Singing upbeat, noisy songs to a grieving heart is just as thoughtless and painful. True love shares in the sorrow of others rather than forcing shallow cheer on them.

When an enemy is hungry or thirsty, we are told to feed him and give him water to drink. Meeting hostility with practical kindness can make an enemy feel the burning sting of shame and melt his anger. The Lord notices this mercy and will reward you for doing good.

differ.view: Showing kindness softens an enemy toward repentance, but if refused, it increases their guilt and brings God's judgment against them.
The burning coals picture love melting an enemy's hardened heart into repentance and kindness, like smelting metal ore.

notes.meaning: Just as a damp north wind gathers clouds and produces rain, a secret gossip brings out angry, troubled faces. When people spread slander behind someone's back, it creates friction and bad feelings all around. An angry look from a listener can also stop a gossiper in their tracks.

It is better to camp on a narrow corner of a flat rooftop, open to the wind and rain, than to share a spacious home with an argumentative spouse. Constant quarreling drains the peace out of a home and makes daily life miserable. A peaceful spirit is essential for a happy family life.

A drink of cold water brings wonderful relief to a traveler who is parched and exhausted from a long journey. Hearing good news about family or friends who are far away brings that same refreshing comfort to an anxious heart. It revives our spirits when we have waited a long time.

A good person should be like a clean spring that offers fresh water and life to an entire town. If a righteous person cowers before evil, compromises his values, or gives in to sin, that pure fountain is muddied and ruined. When godly people yield to wicked pressure, their ability to help others is badly damaged.

Eating too much honey makes a person feel sick, and constantly chasing praise from other people ruins a person's character. Fishing for compliments and trying to build up your own fame is shameful rather than honorable. True honor comes from serving God quietly rather than boasting about yourself.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin Vulgate translation, some understand this as a warning that searching too deeply into divine mysteries will overwhelm human minds with God's majesty.

notes.meaning: In ancient days, a city with knocked-down walls had no protection against invading armies. A person who cannot rule his own temper and desires is completely open to attack from temptation and ruin. Self-control acts like a strong fortress wall that keeps our hearts safe.
